answer:
Start the container with the `--gpus=all` flag, as shown in the Nvidia GPU section of the Docker guide:

```shell
docker run -d --gpus=all -v ollama:/root/.ollama -p 11434:11434 --name ollama ollama/ollama
```

This command is quoted from "docker run -d --gpus=all -v ollama:/root/.ollama -p 11434:11434 --name ollama ollama/ollama" [ollama/docs/docker.md].

Before running it, you need the NVIDIA Container Toolkit installed and Docker configured to use it. The docs say: "sudo nvidia-ctk runtime configure --runtime=docker" followed by "sudo systemctl restart docker" [ollama/docs/docker.md]. Those steps are listed under "Configure Docker to use Nvidia driver."

To confirm the container can see your GPUs, the troubleshooting guide suggests: "Try `docker run --gpus all ubuntu nvidia-smi` - if this doesn't work, Ollama won't be able to see your NVIDIA GPU." [ollama/docs/troubleshooting.md]

The docs also note that if you want Ollama to use only a subset of GPUs, you can set `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`: "If you have multiple NVIDIA GPUs in your system and want to limit Ollama to use a subset, you can set `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` to a comma separated list of GPUs." [ollama/docs/gpu.md]
